title: 2016 Ecuador earthquake
summary: A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck Ecuador's northwestern coast on 16 April 2016, flattening buildings and ravaging towns. The death toll reached 272 within a day, with more than 2,500 injured. States of emergency were declared in six provinces, and at least 135 aftershocks followed. It was reported as the strongest quake to hit Ecuador since 1979.

where.modern_name: Northwestern coast of Ecuador, near Pedernales

importance.justification: Deadly regional earthquake, strongest in Ecuador in decades, with extensive scientific study.

audience_note: Mentions deaths, injuries and people trapped in rubble.

sources.title: Ecuador Earthquake: State of Emergency Declared After at Least 272 Killed

reviewer_note: The ISC lists origin time as 23:58:34 (presumably UTC) on 16 April, while NBC reports local time just before 7 p.m. Death toll of 272 is an early figure from 17 April and may have risen. The ISC source is a bibliography listing, so it supports only the date, location and magnitude. (Drafted by the Wikipedia pipeline from isc.ac.uk, nbcnews.com; quotes machine-checked.)
